title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial (N=150 synthetic intents; shared_initial_candidate semantics) to test whether constrained prompting combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair, one allowed repair) materially increases verifier-level semantic correctness for natural-language → low-level network-configuration translation. Model: gpt-5-mini; verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. For each intent a single initial model generation was shared across baseline and guarded conditions; the guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call if the verifier failed that initial candidate. Results (confirmatory): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.0066667 (0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150); median revision iterations = 0 (IQR = 0). Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus the guarded workflow yielded a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over an already near-ceiling baseline. We bound conclusions to the synthetic corpus, single model, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and deterministic validator and emphasize the methodological lesson that pilot baseline calibration is necessary to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces aim to reduce NetOps friction by translating human operator intents into concrete low-level configuration sequences that can be executed or reviewed. Prior studies show that large language models (LLMs) can produce useful configuration templates but frequently produce syntactic errors, omissions, or unsafe sequences that necessitate downstream correction or verification [1]. Deterministic verifier-guided generate→verify→repair pipelines are a common defensive architecture intended to detect and correct such errors prior to execution [2], while security analyses motivate runtime gating because textual claims may be converted into concrete actions in agentic pipelines, creating claim-to-action vulnerabilities [3], [4].

Research question. After a fresh literature synthesis and a machine-readable preregistration we tested a narrowly scoped confirmatory question: Does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation compared with unconstrained baseline prompting in a paired design? The preregistration (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) and its SHA-256 fingerprint are reported in the Disclosure Statement. Our study explicitly restricts inference to the synthetic verifier-capable task bank used in the run and to the single declared model and deterministic validator used in execution.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial using a deterministic validator as the pass/fail oracle and a shared_initial_candidate execution semantics that isolates the marginal benefit of an allowed single repair. (2) A complete artifactized execution and analysis (N=150 paired tasks; completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151) comparing baseline free-text prompting to constrained-template prompting plus up to one verifier-guided repair. (3) An artifact-grounded empirical outcome: the guarded pipeline produced a negligible numerical improvement (0.67 percentage points) over a near-ceiling baseline; we draw a methodological lesson about pilot baseline calibration for preregistered NetOps trials.
sections.related_work:
Our study intersects three strands of recent literature relevant to LLM-assisted NetOps. First, intent-to-configuration research documents the difficulty of reliably converting free-text operator intents into verifier-sound artifacts and reports modest semantic-correctness rates on public benchmarks [1]. Second, integrated generator-plus-verifier designs and iterative repair approaches demonstrate correctness improvements for infrastructure-as-code and configuration repair tasks when deterministic or policy-guided verifiers are used as feedback or supervision [2], [5]. Third, security and adversarial studies show that multi-tool LLM agents can convert textual claims into harmful actions under certain conditions and that runtime gating and input-hardening are necessary defensive primitives [3], [4].

Positioning. Compared with prior empirical work that reports larger guarded-vs-baseline gains, our trial differs in four controlled ways that materially affect the estimand: (a) shared_initial_candidate execution semantics (a single initial sample was shared across conditions), (b) a one-repair budget per task, (c) a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), and (d) a synthetic verifier-capable task bank limited to small topologies. These design choices intentionally isolate the marginal value of a single deterministic-repair step applied to an identical initial generation, rather than measuring averaged per-condition sampling differences or multi-iteration repair benefit. Our findings therefore complement rather than contradict reports of larger gains under different semantics or repair budgets [2], [5].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory estimand. The trial was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and frozen prior to observing model outputs (preregistration SHA-256 reported in the Disclosure Statement). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where 'guarded' denotes constrained prompting plus up to one verifier-guided repair and 'baseline' denotes free-text prompting. The preregistered primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar, with 95% bootstrap percentile confidence intervals computed from 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Secondary contrasts were preregistered but not used for confirmatory inference in this run.

Execution semantics and their interpretation. The execution contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial model generation was produced and that identical sampled candidate was evaluated under both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call only when the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Consequently, the baseline success rate reported here measures the validity of that single initial sampled candidate; the guarded-vs-baseline contrast therefore isolates the marginal effect of at most one repair applied to the identical initial sample. This interpretation is central to the estimand and is reflected in the deterministic reconciliation and auditing artifacts.

Task bank, sampling, and inclusion/exclusion. Confirmatory tasks: N=150 distinct synthetic intents generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. The task bank was balanced across four intent families: reachability/isolation, ACL-like changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, and uplink switchover patterns. Topology sizes were restricted to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Prior to model calls a deterministic ambiguity detector and parser/verifier-coverage checks were applied; no confirmatory exclusions occurred in this run (exclusions = 0). The preregistered sampling plan and the execution manifest document deterministic generator seeds and task identifiers.

Model, validator, and runtime sampling semantics. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). Verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) implementing a full-intent-constraint boolean pass/fail rule plus a normalized-configuration output used for scoring. Reviewer-requested runtime clarification (incorporated per artifacts): the archived execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). No deterministic sampling temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced; therefore model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. All per-call runtime sampling metadata and provider-call logs were archived and are part of the reproducibility bundle.

Adapter, call budget, and repair policy. The adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforced exactly one initial model call per intent and at most one repair call per intent (planned episodes = 300; maximum_model_calls = 300). Each model call executed in an isolated API session with recorded per-call metadata. The frozen retry policy allowed one deterministic retry for provider/API transient failures; none occurred. The run adhered to the repair budget: model_calls_used = 151 and repair-stage invocations observed = 1.

Scoring and statistical analysis. Primary outcome: deterministic validator pass/fail per intent candidate. Primary analysis used an exact McNemar two-sided test on the paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) and 95% bootstrap percentile CIs computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729), as preregistered. The primary-analysis missingness treatment was 'complete_pair_primary' (complete-pair analysis); no missing or unscorable pairs were observed. Paired-contingency counts and condition summaries are archived and form the analysis inputs.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and audit. Planned paired episodes = 300; completed_episode_count = 300; complete_pair_count = 150. Model calls used = 151 (shared_initial_generation stage_count = 150; repair stage_count = 1). No episodes failed or were excluded; contamination flags = 0. These counts are recorded in deterministic_reconciliation.json and analysis/missingness_summary.csv and confirm adherence to the preregistered execution contract.

Primary numerical outcomes. Paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline): n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). The primary numerical artifacts are analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.

Repair diagnostics and revision iterations. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. Median revision iterations in guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). The single repair converted one initially invalid candidate into a valid configuration according to the deterministic validator; the validator trace for that episode records repair_applied = true and validator.validation_after.valid = true. Provider-call auditing (deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 151 with zero failed calls.

Representative artifact-grounded examples. Representative tasks in the execution bundle illustrate intent structure, required sequences, and validator traces. Example (task-000001): intent = "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the expected four-command sequence; validator_trace.validation_after reports parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, normalized_configuration matching the reference, and valid = true. Similar representative artifacts for tasks 000002–000006 show matched normalized outputs and validator verdicts. These artifact examples and SHA-256s are archived in the execution manifest.

Sensitivity and observed-power implications. The preregistered power calculation targeted detecting an absolute 15 percentage-point increase (e.g., baseline ~35% → guarded 50%) with N=150. Observed baseline ≈99.33% created a ceiling effect that removed most observable room for improvement, invalidating the preregistered power assumptions. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 and the narrow bootstrap CI quantify the limited inferential sensitivity in this run; treating the single repair as a success-improving event yields only a 0.67 pp change with negligible statistical evidence under the planned test.
sections.discussion:
Methodological lesson: baseline calibration. The principal scientific lesson is methodological. Pre-lock power calculations assumed a substantially lower baseline success rate; the unexpectedly high baseline renders the confirmatory contrast uninformative for moderate-to-large effects. We therefore recommend that future preregistered NetOps confirmatory trials include a brief, well-documented pilot to estimate initial-candidate baseline competence for the chosen model and prompt family prior to finalizing sample size and repair budgets.

Interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because identical initial samples were used across conditions, the guarded pipeline's only pathway to improve the paired outcome was the single allowed repair call. Therefore our measured paired difference strictly bounds the marginal benefit of one repair applied to the same initial generation. Alternative semantics—independent per-condition sampling, larger repair budgets, or multi-iteration repair—would estimate different causal contrasts and could yield larger observable differences; these remain important follow-up designs.

Operational implications beyond binary pass/fail. Even when the guarded pipeline yields negligible numerical improvement on a binary verifier pass/fail metric, it still produces operationally useful artifacts: auditable decision records, explicit verifier verdicts usable for operator gating, repair prompts that can be surfaced in operator dashboards, and standardized normalized configurations for downstream automation. These non-statistical benefits are important in practice and are preserved in the archived artifact bundle.

Relation to prior work. Our null-to-small guarded effect does not contradict prior reports of more substantial benefits from verifier-guided repair [2], [5]. Those studies commonly used different semantics (independent sampling), larger repair budgets, or tasks with lower baseline model competence. Our contribution is a tightly bounded measurement of a single-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics with gpt-5-mini on a deterministic synthetic corpus and deterministic validator; the artifacts allow direct comparison of how design choices change empirical outcomes.

Threats to validity. Internal: the shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally restrict inter-condition sampling variance but do not measure per-condition sampling differences. Construct: our binary endpoint is a deterministic validator pass/fail that depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; mapping or validator bugs would bias measurements (the execution bundle includes mapping unit-tests run prior to execution). External: single-model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic tasks, and small topologies (4–32 nodes) limit generalization to production WANs and vendor-specific CLIs. Conclusion validity: preregistered power assumptions were invalidated by the ceiling baseline; reported p-values and CIs accurately reflect this limited inferential power.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting to constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On the archived synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and the deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (0.67 percentage points), a numerically small and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The central scientific recommendation is methodological: preregistered LLM-for-NetOps trials should incorporate brief pilot baseline calibration to align sample size, task difficulty, and repair budgets with observed model competence and to avoid ceiling effects that undermine confirmatory power. Evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, multi-model comparisons, and production-scale topologies are important directions for future work.

Declared model/tooling: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0); adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Runtime sampling semantics (explicit): the archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); no deterministic sampling temperature or fixed random-seed sampling was enforced, and therefore model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. No human manually edited technical content, analyses, figures, captions, or references after the autonomy lock. Key execution facts (archived): completed episodes = 300; complete paired tasks = 150; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. All runtime sampling metadata, provider-call traces, verifier inputs/verdicts, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest; the archived master-prompt reference and preregistration fingerprint above identify the immutable prompts used for the autonomous run.
limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
